successCriteria.description: The barrel export `src/modules/audit/index.ts` exports exactly three symbols: `AuditRecord`, `IAuditService`, `AuditService`. It does NOT export `IAuditRepository` or `AuditRepository`.

`AuditService` has zero imports from `audit.repository.interface` or `audit.repository`. Its only imports are from `src/shared/db/connection.ts`, `./audit.service.interface`, `./audit.model`, and `../../shared/types`.
`AuditService.record()` executes `INSERT INTO audit_records` directly via the shared `pool` (or an optional `PoolClient` passed for transaction support). It does NOT delegate to any repository.
Files `src/modules/audit/audit.repository.interface.ts` and `src/modules/audit/audit.repository.ts` are deleted — they must not exist after this phase.

constraints: The audit module has NO repository. `AuditService` takes the shared `pool` (or `PoolClient`) directly and performs its own SQL. This is an intentional architectural decision recorded in the reconciled architecture: the audit module owns only `AuditRecord`, `IAuditService`, and `AuditService`.

`AuditService` must accept an optional `PoolClient` parameter on `record()` so callers can pass a transaction client. When a client is provided, the service uses it for the INSERT and does NOT release it. When omitted, the service uses the shared pool directly.

The `IAuditService` interface must NOT change its method signature in a way that breaks existing consumers. The `record()` method must still accept `Omit<AuditRecord, 'id' | 'createdAt'>` and return `Promise<AuditRecord>`. The optional transaction client may be added as a second parameter.
outOfScope: Creation or modification of `IAuditRepository`, `AuditRepository`, `audit.repository.interface.ts`, or `audit.repository.ts` — these are artifacts of a prior design being replaced. The audit module must NOT use a repository.

entityInvariants.invariant: Every `AuditRecord` is immutable after creation — it has no update or delete operations. Its `id` is generated server-side (via `gen_random_uuid()` in SQL) and `createdAt` is set to the insertion timestamp (via `NOW()`).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at this layer — the audit service is a cross-cutting utility called by other services that have already performed authorization. The caller is responsible for populating `performedBy` with the authenticated user's ID.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: If the INSERT fails (e.g., constraint violation, connection error), the error propagates to the caller. The service does not swallow or transform database errors.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `AuditRecord` entity shape (fields: `id`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `action`, `performedBy`, `changes`, `createdAt`) must match the definition in `src/modules/audit/audit.model.ts` — no fields added, removed, or renamed.
The `AuditAction` enum used in `AuditRecord.action` must be imported from `src/shared/types/index.ts` — the same source used by all other modules. No local redefinition.

The SQL INSERT in `AuditService.record()` must use the same column names and parameterized query pattern as the existing `AuditRepository.insert()`: `INSERT INTO audit_records (id, entity_type, entity_id, action, performed_by, changes, created_at) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, $3, $4, $5, NOW()) RETURNING ...` with the same column-to-property aliasing (`entity_type AS "entityType"`, etc.).
The shared pool import must use the same path and named export as every other module: `import { pool } from '../../shared/db/connection'`.

integrationPoints.why: AuditService uses the shared PostgreSQL pool for its INSERT — the same pool every other module uses.
